title: Landnam scene script
description: One scene: its type, where it is implemented today, how to open it in the real game, and the game objects it is made of. Web and native read the same declarations.

id.description: Same as the file name and the game route (for example hangar).

type.description: Scene type from shared/engine/scene-types.json. It fixes which slots exist.

name.description: Internal name for tools and tickets. Never shown in the game UI.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences: what the player does here.

tickets.description: Linear tickets that touch this scene. `studio where SSL-123` finds scenes from these.

qa.description: Storyboard and QA scene ids (qa/scenes.json) that show this scene. They carry the native snapshot names, so the Studio can show native beside web.

runtime.description: Where this scene is implemented today.

surface.description: Same vocabulary as web/lib/data/scenes.ts. canvas: a PixiJS surface with data-driven game objects. dom: a React or SwiftUI screen with no object graph yet, still to be migrated.

web.description: Web files that draw this scene, repo-relative.

native.description: Native files that draw this scene, repo-relative.

engine.description: Existing engine scene JSON files, repo-relative.

data.description: Authoring sources this scene reads, relative to shared/authoring/.

preview.description: How the Scene Studio opens this scene in the real game with no login.

route.description: Game screen id. Must be a route of this scene type.

states.description: Game checkpoints to show. These carry the campaign with them (tutorial, balance, prompts), so they are tucked away; presets are the way to look at a scene.

things.description: Everything that can be in this scene. Switch things on in the Studio to see them in the real game, then save the combination as a preset.

presets.description: Named setups of this scene: which things are on, with plain-language instructions for whoever tests or builds it. Every agent reads them.

objects.description: The scene's game objects as a flat list. `parent` builds the tree.

rect.description: Rectangle in the 0 to 1 safe-area space of the scene.

patch.description: Shallow-merged into the player after load, to reach states no fixture covers.

id.description: Stable name, unique in the scene.

kind.description: What sort of game object this is.

parent.description: Id of the object this one belongs to. Leave out for a top-level object.

slot.description: Fixed place in the scene type. The same slot is in the same place on web and native.

prefab.description: Reusable object this one is an instance of, such as shared-hud.

asset.description: Data or art file this object loads, repo-relative.

components.description: Behaviours, such as Clickable or Movable.

bindings.description: What game state this object reads or writes.

label.description: Text on the object, when it has any.

status.description: implemented: exists in the game. proposed: drawn in the Studio as a request for an agent to build.

id.description: Stable name, unique in the scene. Presets refer to it.

group.description: The heading it is listed under, such as Structures or Time of day.

exclusive.description: Things that share a value here are choices: only one of them can be on.

state.description: Game state to layer over the scene's starting point while this is on. Tables merge, lists gain entries, anything else is replaced. Keys are checked against the game's own state. "@now-30s" and "@now+2h" mean an instant relative to now.

query.description: Switches of the stage page. Several things that set the same key are joined with commas.

time.description: Time of day over the base.

sky.description: Sky events and weather to force: meteors, launch, balloon, satellite, aurora, comet, eclipse, venus, clear, cloudy, windy, rain, storm, fog.

shower.description: Show the Orionids event, which is otherwise only seen in its real dates.

hud.description: Show the base's clock and balance, which the sandbox hides.

building.description: Focus a building on the base, such as hangar.

launchscene.description: Start the launch sequence on the launchpad.

click.description: data-testid values to click, in order, once the scene has loaded. Reaches states that need an action.

range.description: Makes this a slider, which is always applied. Use {value} and {rest} (max minus value) inside strings in `state`.

id.description: Stable name, unique in the scene. Flows refer to it.

things.description: Ids of the things that are on. Leave this out to start from the scene's defaults.

values.description: Where each slider sits, by thing id.

instructions.description: Plain language: what to try here, what should happen, what must not. Agents treat it as the test for this setup.
